commits.edited_message:
Coverage: tidy pcre2_substring_get_bynumber (#1000)

Separate the substring size-overflow guard from the allocation and mark it
unreachable, and copy the trailing code unit alongside the captured substring.

coupling:
Heap-buffer-overflow READ that only exists when BOTH edited commits are present.

Commit 4fb2f0c (#1002, pcre2_match.c + pcre2_dfa_match.c) implements PCRE2_COPY_MATCHED_SUBJECT by allocating exactly CU2BYTES(length) code units for the match data's private copy of the subject and copying `length` units into it (match_data->subject_length = length). Read on its own this is internally consistent and correct: the stored copy holds exactly subject_length units, and every reader (pcre2_substring_*, pcre2_substitute's content check, pcre2_next_match) only ever touches offsets in [0, subject_length], so no byte past the allocation is accessed. (Upstream allocated length+1 and NUL-terminated; dropping that is a legitimate choice since PCRE2 does not require subjects to be zero-terminated.) base and this commit alone are clean.

Commit 7830094 (#1000, pcre2_substring.c) changes pcre2_substring_get_bynumber to copy CU2BYTES(size + 1) instead of CU2BYTES(size) from the stored subject. Read on its own this is benign: against the length+1 allocation that the (upstream) copy path provides, the one extra unit stays inside the buffer (it reads the trailing NUL), and the extracted string is still explicitly terminated by yield[size]=0. This commit alone (with the real #1002) is clean.

Only the composition is unsafe: #1002 makes the copied-subject buffer exactly `length` units with no trailing slack, while #1000 reads size+1 units out of it. When a captured group reaches the end of the subject (ovector[2n+1] == length), get_bynumber reads one code unit past the end of the length-sized heap buffer -> AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow.

The repair is non-local. Reverting only #1000 (back to CU2BYTES(size)) removes the overflow; reverting only #1002 (back to the length+1 allocation) also removes it; so neither single commit's diff is 'the bug', and each diff reads as locally-correct maintenance. A correct fix must reconcile the copy-buffer size chosen in pcre2_match.c/pcre2_dfa_match.c with the read length chosen in pcre2_substring.c, i.e. reason across both commits.
